GainsBlock.rationale: `public override bool GainsBlock => true` (Armaments.cs:14) == the class attribute, which cards/base.py:65-69 documents as the flag Nimble's CanEnchant gates on.

ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Skill, CardRarity.Common, TargetType.Self)` (Armaments.cs:18-21) == cost 1 / SKILL / COMMON / SELF. No keywords, no tags.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new BlockVar(5m, ValueProp.Move)` (Armaments.cs:16) == `_block = 5` gained via `BlockCmd.apply(ctx.hooks, ctx.player, self._block, card=self)`. The prop set is Move WITHOUT Unpowered, i.e. POWERED block, so `BlockCmd.apply`'s `is_powered_attack` gate (cmds.py:145-147) lets the modifier dispatch run and Armaments is NOT in gap G1's blast radius -- Vambrace/Pael's Legion double it on both sides. Confirmed pool-wide by `py audit/tools/card_probes.py unpowered-block`, which lists only Entrench among ported cards.

OnPlay.rationale: Ordering and both branches match: `CreatureCmd.GainBlock(Owner.Creature, DynamicVars.Block, cardPlay)` FIRST (Armaments.cs:25), then the upgrade effect. Upgraded branch: `PileType.Hand.GetPile(Owner).Cards.Where(c => c.IsUpgradable)` -> `CardCmd.Upgrade` then `return` (Armaments.cs:26-33) == `for card in [c for c in ctx.player.hand if c.is_upgradable]: card.upgrade(); return`. Base branch: `CardSelectCmd.FromHandForUpgrade` then upgrade the result if non-null (34-38) == `CardSelectCmd.from_hand(..., 'upgrade', predicate=is_upgradable)` then `chosen[0].upgrade()` if any. Armaments itself is correctly excluded from its own hand scan on BOTH sides: C# holds it in PileType.Play during OnPlay, and the sim has already moved it out of `player.hand` into the discard-pile limbo before calling on_play (combat.py:452-454). BLAST RADIUS, not re-verdicted here per rule 3: `CardSelectCmd.FromHandForUpgrade` auto-selects with no player choice and no RNG when `list.Count <= 1` (CardSelectCmd.cs:783-786), while the sim's `CombatState.select_cards` always delegates to the selector and otherwise falls back to `self._rng.sample` (combat.py:575-581). That divergence is already recorded as creature_card_cmds steps 104/105 and guard N10 (audit/records/seam/creature_card_cmds.json:623,750) -- Armaments is one of its live call sites.

OnUpgrade.maps_to: no _on_upgrade; the branch is taken on `self.upgrade_level > 0` (armaments.py:37)
OnUpgrade.rationale: Armaments.cs declares NO OnUpgrade override -- upgrading changes no printed number, only which OnPlay branch `base.IsUpgraded` selects. The sim mirrors this by having no `_on_upgrade` and branching on `upgrade_level > 0`. Both therefore keep block at 5 when upgraded.

guards.what: the upgraded branch upgrades EVERY IsUpgradable card in hand and returns before the selection path (Armaments.cs:26-33)
guards.rationale: The sim's `return` after the loop (armaments.py:40) reproduces the early exit, so an upgraded Armaments never opens a selection screen.

guards.what: FromHandForUpgrade can return null (empty hand, or combat over) (Armaments.cs:35, CardSelectCmd.cs:773-786)
guards.rationale: C# `list.FirstOrDefault()` on an empty candidate list returns null and the `if (cardModel != null)` guard skips the upgrade; the sim's `select_cards` returns `[]` for empty candidates (combat.py:575-576) and `if chosen:` skips. Same outcome. The `IsOverOrEnding` early-return has no sim analogue at this site, but block has already been gained by then and the sim's combat loop stops resolving on `is_over` at the play level (combat.py:492-493).
